issues.description: Deprecation message omits the recommended replacement signature nuance for stderr-only callers
issues.detail: The message says 'use contextlib.redirect_stdout and contextlib.redirect_stderr instead' but `redirected` accepts both simultaneously. Users redirecting both streams must now nest two context managers. A one-line example or note in the deprecation message and docstring would prevent confusion during migration.
The Sphinx `.. deprecated:: 4.3` block says 'Use the stlib's' — should be 'stdlib's'. Minor but visible in rendered docs once this release ships.

Falcon's towncrier config typically distinguishes deprecations from misc changes so users scanning the changelog see them. A deprecation warning that schedules removal in 5.0 is more discoverable under a deprecation/removal fragment type than under misc.

issues.description: New test does not assert the deprecation warning is raised exactly once
issues.detail: `pytest.warns` passes if any matching warning occurs. If `@deprecated` somehow fires multiple times (e.g., on re-entry), the test won't catch it. Consider `with pytest.warns(...) as record:` and asserting `len(record) == 1` for tighter coverage of the deprecation contract.

issues.description: Import ordering in test file may violate project isort convention
issues.detail: `import contextlib` is placed between `from argparse import Namespace` and `import io`. Falcon typically groups stdlib imports alphabetically with `from` imports separate. Worth running the project's isort/ruff config to confirm this passes CI lint before merge.

review.summary: This is a small, well-scoped deprecation PR that correctly wires `@falcon.util.deprecated`, updates internal tests to use the stdlib replacement, and adds a deprecation test plus newsfragment. Main concerns are minor: a docstring typo ('stlib'), a possibly mis-categorized newsfragment (`.misc` vs deprecation), and a deprecation message that doesn't clarify how to handle the combined-streams use case. Nothing blocks merge; the changes are straightforward and behavior-preserving for the still-supported `redirected` path.
